description: CP-CHECK-1 vectors (kernel 2.0.0, PROPOSED). regex-vectors: the I-Regexp dialect (RFC 9485 ABNF) - valid patterns with strings that must and must not match WHOLE-value, and patterns every implementation must refuse, each with why; several are dialect traps where Python re, .NET or ECMAScript would answer differently. verdict-vectors: check-verdict (B.1.10) over {check (observes, criteria, applies-when?, each?), observation, parameters?} -> one of satisfied | not-satisfied | inconclusive | not-applicable; strong Kleene AND; an unbound parameter is inconclusive (D9). aggregate-vectors: Assessment.result from row outcomes (CHECK-10). object-vectors: closed shapes - an object must match exactly the named type, or none. bundle-vectors: the CHECK-n rule ids a conformant tool names for the bundle (exact set; expected-notes are substrings of notes); `store` is an in-memory evidence store, path -> UTF-8 text. Check digests are semantic digests computed by the reference canonical form; editing a vector Check without recomputing its digest makes CHECK-8 fire.

regex-vectors.why: whole-value and case-sensitive: no implicit substring search, no case folding
'.' is any character but \n AND \r (XSD); Python re and PCRE let \r through
^ and $ are ordinary characters in I-Regexp - matching is whole-value already
the explicit range is ASCII digits only
XSD \d means \p{Nd} - the reason I-Regexp drops \d: hosts disagree
nested stars: exponential for a backtracking engine, linear for a state-set engine
character-class subtraction (XSD has it, I-Regexp does not)

verdict-vectors.name: a JSON true is not an integer
a string is not an integer
decimals compare by value, never as floats
a JSON float is not a decimal fact
a non-canonical decimal is not a decimal fact
present fails - an absent fact is observed-absent
subset-of the empty list: the list must be empty
subset-of the empty list fails on any element
matches is not a substring search
matches on a list: every element
matches-not on a list: no element
a value beyond the input limit is not matched
no observation at all is inconclusive
an undeclared fact in criteria is inconclusive
unbound parameter - a default is never substituted (D9)
tailoring A binds 6: the observation 5 passes
tailoring B binds 4: the SAME observation 5 fails
a bound value of the wrong type is inconclusive
Kleene: one definite failure decides over a missing fact
Kleene: a missing fact and a pass are inconclusive
each + applies-when: nothing applicable, allow-empty false

object-vectors.name: a Check without collectors (manual collection, still recomputable)
a JSON float never enters a check (decimals are canonical strings)
an operator outside the closed set
closed shape: code is never a kernel field
observation inline OR by reference, not both
a result time is RFC 3339 date-time
outcomes are closed: an error is inconclusive with a reason
an observation is facts OR resources
a Finding names the check that raised it
